# Review — odyssey-076 (15.454–557)

Reviewer: adversarial, two passes. `t` untouched (checked: every `t` identical to the draft, and the `t` of all 63 units joined reproduce the packet's 104 lines; `ln` and `p` flags match the packet; `l` and `t` have the same number of lines; no `\n` in `i`; no `tr` or `sc`). No scansion flags in the packet, so there was nothing to scan by hand. Edited `units.json` and `gloss.json` in place by script.

## Pass 1 — notes, Greek → l, l ↔ i, remembered English, quotation marks

Method: each note read against its own unit's Greek, `l` and `i`; every positional claim ("begins/ends in the middle of line N", "line N", "the next unit", "of 460/497/496/517/481") checked against the packet; every grammatical label checked; Greek → `l` word by word; `l` ↔ `i` for sense and force; `i` read for phrases that arrive ready-made; house table (conventions.md) searched for every epithet and formula in the part; repeated lines compared with the packet's published English.

### Checked and found sound (no change)

- Quotation marks. Eumaeus's speech runs on from odyssey-075 (its last unit closes only the inner ’ of the woman's speech): unit 454 correctly has no opening “ and no `mark`; the closing ” is on 484 in `l` and `i`. Speeches 486–492, 503–507, 509–511, 513–524, 531–534, 536–538, 540–543, 545–546: “ on first unit, ” on last, `mark` on the first, in both layers; no other “ ” anywhere; the narrator's 539 correctly stands as its own unit. `p` on exactly the ten ¶ lines.
- Whole-unit repeats 508, 512, 535: `l` and `i` identical to the published ones. Partial repeats 471, 476, 477, 493, 501, 502, 525, 548, 554: wording of the repeated line matches the packet.
- Positional claims: all "begins/ends in the middle of line N" notes (463, 468, 470, 475, 481, 491, 495, 509, 514, 516, 526, 552), the cross-references (459, 460, 481, 496, 497, 517, 512/535, 514/546, 522/554, 488, 15.390) are true of the lines.
- House table: ἐνδυκέως, ἤπια, ὑγρὰ κέλευθα, πότνια μήτηρ, δμῳαί, ἐσάντα, ἄντλος, πρόδομος, κοιρανέουσι, ἰοχέαιρα, ἐΰθρονος, ἀγλαός, κλυτός, διογενής, πεπνυμένος reply-formula, ἦ καί, ἔν τ’ ἄρα οἱ φῦ χειρί, ἱστός/ἱστία, ὠκύαλος, γέρας, αἴθοπα οἶνον, αἲ γάρ, δουρικλειτός: all agree with the rows. Only καρτερός broke its row (fixed above).
- Remembered English: none found. Phrases that could look ready-made ("strung with beads of amber", "the swift-sailing ship", "sea of … harvest" type) are table renderings or built from the cases.

### Considered and refused (Pass 1)

- 2 l/i "beads" for ἠλέκτροισιν: Greek is a plural of ἤλεκτρον (pieces of amber on a necklace); the note says so. Kept.
- 20 i "by telling me each of these things": "me" is not in the Greek but λέγων is addressed to him (μοι earlier); harmless English. Kept.
- 37 i "I would myself bid you" for ἐγώ γε (l "I at least"): γε is limiting/intensifying; "myself" carries the same stress in prose. Kept.
- 43 l "aether": a loanword where the table has no row; the note says what it is and `i` has "bright upper air". Kept.
- 45 note "The feathers land right in front of Telemachus": a paraphrase of μεσσηγὺς νηός τε καὶ αὐτοῦ Τηλεμάχοιο; does not contradict `l`/`i`. Kept.
- 48 i drops ἀλλά (l has "but"): the semicolon carries the contrast in English prose; adding "on the contrary" would overtranslate. Kept.
- 56 μίμνοι with σύ (the printed ending is the 3 sg. -οι, not 2 sg. -οις): the glossary entry records the oddity; the note's translation is unaffected. No note sentence added. Kept as printed.
- 56 reading of εἰ γάρ as "even if" rather than a wish: drafter flagged it; the note gives the grammar and the English follows the apodosis (κομιῶ). Kept.
- 25 i "at the shore" beside l "on the dry land" for ἐπὶ χέρσου (drafter's point 12): note says explicitly that the Greek does not say whether the keel has touched. Kept.
- 58 κληΐς "rowing-benches": differs from the table's row 629 (πολυκλήιδι "many thwarts") and from the shipped `i` "oarlocks" of odyssey-062 and -073 (which is a mistranslation: oarlocks are not benches). The new-renderings table records the choice and why. Kept; flagged for the owner (see unresolved).
- 8 note "here a child's" (lack of understanding): an interpretive gloss, not a grammatical label; true of the context. Kept.
- 14 κήξ "sea-bird" in `i` and "kex" in `l`: species unknown, note says so. Kept.
- Part title and `about`: title kept; `about` corrected only where it said "won over, the pair".

## Pass 2 — re-check, then every parse in gloss.json against its line(s)

Re-read all 63 units after the Pass 1 edits (no new problem; the changed notes read true against `l`/`i`). Then each of the 102 novel entries read against every line in which the form occurs; each of the 8 broadened entries checked to begin with the existing entry whole; each known form checked for whether its existing entry covers its use here (all 431 read). Format checks by script: no novel entry ≥ 230 characters, none with an ASCII apostrophe or backtick, none with a line number or "here". (The broadened entries exceed 230 characters by construction: old entry whole plus the new reading.)

### Changes (gloss.json)

| form · kind | severity | what was wrong → what was done |
|---|---|---|
| καρτεροὶ · replaced | low | "mighty" is reserved for ὄβριμος in the house table; καρτερός is "strong" |
| καδδραθέτην · replaced | medium | called "augmented", but the form has no augment (the Attic equivalent κατεδραθέτην has it) |
| εἰναλίη · replaced | medium | called "two-ending adj." but the form is the -η feminine, so the label is false of it |
| πείθῃ · replaced | high | parsed as imperative and as taking the genitive; in the line it is the indicative "you obey" with the dative μοι |
| προβιβάντα · replaced | medium | Attic equivalent was given as the same form προβιβάντα, which is not Attic |
| τελευτήσει · replaced | low | entry fixed it as intransitive, but the note to the line leaves open subject or object (ἦμαρ is neuter) |
| ἠπίου · replaced | low | said "used as a noun", but in the line it agrees with ἀνδρός (the note says so) |
| ἔκφερεν · replaced | low | "epic -εν" misdescribed the ν-movable, which Attic has too |
| ὅρμον · replaced | low | derivation reversed: ὁρμίζω is formed from ὅρμος |
| ἤχθετο · broadened | medium | known entry covers only ἔχθομαι "was hateful to"; the use here is ἄχθομαι of a ship, as the note says |
| κεν · broadened | medium | the κεν entry lacked the εἰς ὅ κεν + subj. use (it stood only under κε) |
| ἰθακήσιοι · broadened | medium | known entry gave only the vocative; the use here is nominative, subject of εἰσορόωσι |
| εἰσορόωσι · broadened | medium | known entry gave only the dative-plural participle; the use here is a finite verb |

Totals, Pass 2: high 1 (πείθῃ); medium 7 (καδδραθέτην, εἰναλίη, προβιβάντα, and the four added broadenings ἤχθετο, κεν, ἰθακήσιοι, εἰσορόωσι); low 5 (καρτεροὶ, τελευτήσει, ἠπίου, ἔκφερεν, ὅρμον).

Old → new for the replaced entries:

- καρτεροὶ: was “καρτερός — strong, mighty; masc. nom. pl., epic (= Attic κρατεροί)” ; now “καρτερός — strong, powerful; masc. nom. pl., epic (= Attic κρατεροί)”
- καδδραθέτην: was “καταδαρθάνω — fall asleep; aor. 3 dual, κατά assimilated to καδ- before δ, augmented (= Attic κατεδραθέτην)” ; now “καταδαρθάνω — fall asleep; aor. 3 dual, κατά assimilated to καδ- before δ, unaugmented (= Attic κατεδραθέτην)”
- εἰναλίη: was “εἰνάλιος — of the sea, sea-dwelling; fem. nom. sg., two-ending adj. (= Attic ἐνάλιος)” ; now “εἰνάλιος — of the sea, sea-dwelling; fem. nom. sg., epic with lengthened first syllable (= Attic ἐνάλιος)”
- πείθῃ: was “πείθομαι — obey, heed (+ gen.); pres. imper. mid. 2 sg. (= Attic πείθου)” ; now “πείθομαι — obey, heed (+ dat.); pres. ind. mid. 2 sg. (the uncontracted form is πείθεαι)”
- προβιβάντα: was “προβιβάω — stride forward; pres. part. masc. acc. sg., epic (= Attic προβιβάντα from βιβάς)” ; now “προβιβάω — stride forward; pres. part. masc. acc. sg., epic (= Attic προβαίνοντα)”
- τελευτήσει: was “τελευτάω — accomplish, come to pass; fut. 3 sg. (or short-vowel aor. subj. after κε), intrans.: ’will come to pass’” ; now “τελευτάω — accomplish, bring to pass; fut. 3 sg. (or short-vowel aor. subj. after κε); trans. ’will bring about’ or intrans. ’will come to pass’”
- ἠπίου: was “ἤπιος — gentle, kindly; masc. gen. sg., used as a noun: ’of a kindly one’” ; now “ἤπιος — gentle, kindly; masc. gen. sg., agreeing with ἀνδρός”
- ἔκφερεν: was “ἐκφέρω — carry out; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented, epic -εν (= Attic ἐξέφερε)” ; now “ἐκφέρω — carry out; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented, ν-movable (= Attic ἐξέφερε)”
- ὅρμον: was “ὅρμος — necklace (from εἴρω ’string’); masc. acc. sg. · also ὅρμος — anchorage, roadstead (from ὁρμίζω ’bring to anchor’); masc. acc. sg.” ; now “ὅρμος — necklace (from εἴρω ’string’); masc. acc. sg. · also ὅρμος — anchorage, roadstead (cf. ὁρμίζω ’bring to anchor’); masc. acc. sg.”

### Considered and refused (Pass 2)

- μίμνοι "pres. opt., agreeing with σύ, 2 sg. (the form is -οι for -οις)": states the oddity correctly. Kept.
- κερῶντό "(= Attic ἐκεράννυντο)": lemma κεράννυμι with the epic κεράομαι contraction named; correct. Kept (the unit note had it backwards, fixed in Pass 1).
- κάτειμι lemma κατέρχομαι with κάτ-ειμι named: acceptable, the parse is right. Kept.
- ἀναβησάμενοι "(= Attic ἀναβιβασάμενοι)", ἧκαν "(Attic has εἷσαν)", πρόμολον "(= Attic προὔμολον)": equivalences are formal and true. Kept.
- τόνδε (known entry says "agreeing with ἄεθλον"): pinned to an earlier line but the parse "acc. sg." is right for 546; not rewritten (never rewrite an existing entry otherwise).
- πολλὰ / πολλά (known): the grave-accent entry already has "greatly" for 489 and the adjectival uses; the acute form is broadened by the glosser for 537. Kept.
- ὑπερωΐῳ "epic with diaeresis", ἐνίαυεν "ν-movable", ἴαλλεν "unaugmented": true of the forms. Kept.
- Broadened entries exceed 230 characters: unavoidable (old entry whole plus new reading). Kept.
